notes: USMLE Content Outline 2026 explicitly lists syringomyelia under spinal cord disorders.

Current 2026 NCBI neuroanatomy guidance identifies the anterior white commissure as containing decussating pain/temperature spinothalamic fibers and describes syringomyelia as an early lesion of these fibers.
Current NCBI Syringomyelia guidance independently supports dissociated pain/temperature loss with early preservation of posterior-column modalities.
An earlier narcolepsy/orexin Q0666 draft was rejected before audit after the post-stage report detected direct canonical overlap with Q0224.

blueprint.system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
official_outline_path: Disorders relating to the spine, spinal cord, and spinal nerve roots

duplicate_gate.narcolepsy_post_stage_rejected_overlap: Q0224 directly covers narcolepsy type 1 due to loss of hypothalamic hypocretin/orexin neurons.
duplicate_gate.replacement_construct: Syringomyelia with anterior white commissure involvement

option_audit.anterior_white_commissure: Uniquely explains selective bilateral pain/temperature loss from a central cervical syrinx.
option_audit.dorsal_columns: Would impair vibration/proprioception, which are preserved.
option_audit.lateral_corticospinal: Would produce motor/upper-motor-neuron deficits rather than isolated dissociated sensory loss.
option_audit.dorsal_root_ganglia: A multilevel bilateral DRG process would not selectively spare non-spinothalamic modalities in this central-cord pattern.
option_audit.medial_lemniscus: Carries dorsal-column modalities after medullary decussation, which are preserved.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A small central cervical syrinx first reaches the anterior white commissure, where second-order pain/temperature fibers cross. This creates bilateral segmental dissociated sensory loss while dorsal columns remain intact.
adversarial_second_pass.dorsal_column_attack: Preserved vibration and joint position directly oppose a dorsal-column lesion.
adversarial_second_pass.motor_attack: Normal strength/reflexes and the modality-specific deficit oppose corticospinal injury as the primary lesion.
adversarial_second_pass.peripheral_attack: A peripheral/DRG process would not produce the classic central crossing-fiber dissociation shown with an MRI-proven syrinx.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No syrinx diameter, spinal level threshold, progression rate, or treatment parameter is asserted.
